subject: Post-demo privacy: binding clauses, subprocessor notify & breach paths
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@medixhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-25T14:30:00Z
Subject: Post-demo privacy: binding clauses, subprocessor notify & breach paths

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the demo time today — really appreciate the detailed questions from your engineering and legal teams. Per our discussion, I wanted to consolidate the open privacy/DPA items so you have a single reference and we can move toward a clean redline: 

Key asks from Medix Health I heard during the call:
- Confirm whether Redwood will be classified as Processor or Controller for the integration we demoed (data flow: patient inputs -> Medix sync -> Redwood inference -> Medix returns).
- Desired breach notification window: you mentioned a preference for 72 hours to controller notification.
- Subprocessor transparency: Medix requested a 30-day notification prior to onboarding new subprocessors with a right to object.
- Log retention and debug access: clarify what logs we retain and retention periods for request/response logs and KV cache traces.
- Data residency: options for EU/US residency and whether specific tenants can be pinned.

Next steps from Redwood (we can action after you confirm priorities):
1) Share our standard DPA and a one-page matrix that maps controller/processor responsibilities for this specific integration.
2) Provide SOC 2 Type II report and an evidence package (encryption at rest/in transit details).
3) Propose redline language for subprocessor notification and breach timing that balances your requirements and our operational constraints.
4) Schedule a 30-minute legal sync next week to walk legal redlines.

If you want to loop in someone from Procurement or InfoSec now, please reply-all with their preferred availability. I attached a brief one-pager that maps the demo data flow for clarity.

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Executive 
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-demo-dataflow-onepager.pdf (diagram stub)

From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@medixhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Medix Health Legal <legal@medixhealth.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-26T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo privacy: binding clauses, subprocessor notify & breach paths

Marcus — thanks for the recap and the diagram. Helpful. A few clarifications from Legal so we can triage: 

1) Controller/Processor: For our use case Medix will be Controller. We expect Redwood to be Processor for processing on behalf of Medix. Please confirm you accept processor obligations (including acting only on our documented instructions).

2) Breach notification: our standard is 72 hours from discovery to notify the Controller; we understand there may be emergency/operational constraints but ask Redwood to commit to that timeline or propose an alternate SLA.

3) Subprocessors: Medix requires 30 calendar days' prior written notice and a right to object to new subprocessors that would process patient data; in practice we use objection only for high-risk subprocessors (e.g., hosting in a new jurisdiction). If you have an existing published subprocessor list, please send it.

4) Logs & retention: please confirm retention windows for request logs, request metadata and any persisted KV cache. Our InfoSec prefers 12 months of logs for auditability unless there's a space/PII concern.

5) SOC2 + encryption: can you provide your latest SOC2 report and a short attestation on encryption in transit and at rest (algorithms, key management). We attached our checklist for reference.

We can do a legal sync next Tue or Wed (AM PT).

-Elena
Director, Product Security
Medix Health

Attachment: Medix-privacy-checklist.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-26T15:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo privacy: binding clauses, subprocessor notify & breach paths

Quick internal note / proposed language before we send to Medix: 

- Controller/Processor line: "For the services covered by this Addendum, Customer (Medix Health) is the Controller and Redwood Inference is the Processor acting solely on the documented instructions of Customer with respect to Personal Data."

- Breach notification: We prefer to commit to "notify without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of becoming aware of a Security Incident affecting Customer Personal Data" with a pragmatic carve for "operational or investigatory limitations" that may push certain details beyond 72 hours, provided initial notification and mitigation steps are communicated. This keeps commercial parity while being realistic.

- Subprocessors: We can agree to publish an up-to-date subprocessor list and provide 30 days' notice for new subprocessors. For high-risk subprocessors in new jurisdictions we can add a step for discussion and temporary mitigation measures; we should avoid a full veto right that blocks necessary infra changes.

- Logs: Default retention for request logs = 12 months; we can offer tiered retention and an option for shorter retention upon request for specific tenants. KV cache: not persisted beyond session except where customer explicitly requests pinned storage; we should flag any feature that persists model context.

Attachments I'm preparing: a proposed redline (proposed-dpa-redline.pdf) with the clauses above and a short cover note. I'll attach SOC2 link separately (we host the latest report on our portal).

-Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-dpa-redline.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@medixhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-27T09:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo privacy: binding clauses, subprocessor notify & breach paths

Elena — thanks for the detail and the checklist. Putting next steps here so we’re aligned: 

Action items from Redwood:
- Share proposed DPA redline (attached) that accepts Processor role, includes the 72-hour initial notification language with the investigatory carve, and publishes a subprocessor notice process. (Attachment: redwood-dpa-proposed-redline-20280727.pdf)
- Send SOC2 access link: https://rwd.in/soc2/medix-report-2028 (link below).
- Provide a short technical note on encryption and key management we can hand to InfoSec.
- Schedule 30-minute legal sync — proposed slots: Tue 2028-07-31 09:00-09:30 PT or Wed 2028-08-01 08:30-09:00 PT. Let us know which works and we’ll send a calendar invite.

If those slots don’t work, propose alternative times and we’ll accommodate. Looking forward to closing the DPA redline quickly.

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-dpa-proposed-redline-20280727.pdf
